newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sundiro to buy plant on B proceeds.
newsitem.headline: Sundiro to buy plant on B proceeds.

text.p: China's Hainan Sundiro Motorcycle Co Ltd will use part of the proceeds raised in its planned 150 million B share offer to buy Hainan Automobile Factory, a company official said on Tuesday.

Sundiro, one of the largest motorcycle makers in China, planned to buy a controlling stake in the factory and make it into a limited firm with registered capital of 700 million yuan, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

Sundiro will hold a 60 percent stake in the company, while another Hainan-based car firm would have the remaining 40 percent, the official said. She declined to say how much Sundiro would pay for the Hainan car factory.
The factory is currently negotiating with Mercedes-Benz DIAG.F to build multi-purpose vans, the official said.

Sundiro, which now has domestic A shares listed on the Shenzhen stock exchange, is about to issue 150 million foreign currency B shares for listing on the Shenzhen bourse as well in 1997 but an issue date has yet to be announced.
Sundiro has said it would mainly use the B share proceeds to upgrade production technology and set up a joint venture with Japanese firm Kawasaki to make motorbike engines.
"The Hainan car factory acquisition will become Sundiro's additional investment with the B share proceeds, pending shareholders' approval at a meeting on July 10," the official said.

Sundiro's B share issue application is being reviewed by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the securities watchdog, and the firm hopes to offer another 20 million B shares if the first-tranche offer is oversubscribed, she said.
Sundiro has named China Cinda Trust and Investment Corp as the domestic chief underwriter and ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett as the international consultant, the official said.
A Sundiro spokesman ealier said the B share offer would carry a P/E ratio of about eight times based on targeted net profits of about 250 million yuan for 1997.
Sundiro posted net profits of 219 million yuan in 1996 against 70.55 million yunn in 1995 based on Chinese accounting standards. It did not give figures based on international standards.

Sundiro, one of the 33 companies recently selected by Beijing as the latest batch of candidates to issue B shares, has a production target of 600,000 to 800,000 motorcycles this year, compared with 350,000 in 1996, the spokesman said.
At the end of 1996, Sundiro had outstanding shares of just over 237 million, composed of 142 million institutional shares, 95 million A shares and 72,240 shares held by staff.
